Question: What do you like to do when you are feeling low?
Old_Answer: I plan. I set higher targets for myself. We tend to feel low when things don't go our way. Failures and disappointments are part of life and there should be a way to deal with it. One need break and recreation time to remain but I know when I deserve that break and when I don't. I can't chill watching a movie when I know I haven't completed my targets for the week. See, I can watch a movie, go for an outing, do an episode of emotional eating. There are innumerable ways, but I believe this will distract me for a while but at the of the day, I will have to face the reality and deal with it. There can be any sort of reason for me feeling low. Personal, emotional, academical or whatever. These failures and disappointment ignites something inside and I become more goal oriented. I find my motivation in my failures. I find motivation in rejections. I find motivation in humiliation. I find motivation in disappointments. I find motivation in awkwardness. I find motivation in silence. Negatives get inside me and push me to work harder than before. Constant self doubt and fear of failure keeps me going. Your past situation should never be a deciding factor for your tomorrow. Constantly work on changing your present, so that your tomorrow can be better. If you get comfortable in your present circumstances you will never be able to grow. There is always something inside me that wants change in my current situation and because I want that change, I consciously work for it. Rabiya

Sometimes, I write about my day, the mundane moments that feel like a burden, and other times, I let my imagination take flight, crafting stories that transport me to different worlds. Whether it’s a soothing melody that calms my racing heart or an upbeat track that lifts my spirits, music has a magical way of reaching the parts of me that feel distant. I try to reconnect with nature too, going for long walks where the wind brushes against my skin and the world feels alive again. In those moments, I find peace in the simplicity of life around me—the rustling leaves, the chirping birds, and the gentle warmth of the sun. It’s a reminder that every low is temporary, just like the ebb and flow of tides. Ultimately, I remind myself that it’s okay to feel this way; I embrace it, knowing that these moments are an essential part of my journey. Rabiya 💕

Answer_with_writing_sample: Do marks really matter in life? Ah, the age-old question that tends to linger in the minds of many students, parents, and educators alike. I have experienced the pressure of chasing grades, pouring countless hours into studying, sometimes sacrificing my mental well-being in the process. I’ve felt that exhilarating rush of achieving high marks, yet I’ve also faced the crushing disappointment of receiving a less-than-ideal score. Through my own journey, I've come to realize that marks are merely a reflection of our performance at a given moment, surrounded by a multitude of variables. They do not define our intelligence, creativity, or our capacity to adapt and grow. What truly matters is the knowledge we gain, the experiences we accumulate, and the resilience we build along the way. Life is a tapestry woven from various threads—our passions, interests, and relationships—none of which can be quantified by numbers on a report card. Learning is a lifelong adventure, and while grades may open doors, it is our character, our values, and our drive that ultimately pave the way to fulfillment. So, while it’s natural to strive for good marks, don’t let them overshadow the beauty of the journey itself. Embrace every moment, every lesson learned, and remember that life is so much more than just numbers. Rabiya 💕
